I am applying for the part-time Mental Health Program Coordinator position. The best part of my day, even amid the chaos, was connecting with my students and listening with an open heart to their troubles and concerns; I became their safe space and sounding board. They shone a light on my path and confirmed how much I want to work with teens. These students lit a fire inside me and gave me clarity of purpose.
Additionally, I am pursuing a bachelor’s degree in psychology at Southern New Hampshire University, with concentrations in Mental Health Counseling and Child and Adolescent Development. I will graduate by the end of 2027, and next fall I will apply to a PsyD program to follow my dream of becoming a clinical psychologist. I understand the boundaries of a non-clinical position and the importance of promptly bringing safety concerns to the clinical team.
In this Mental Health Program Coordinator role, I would bring bilingual (Spanish) communication skills, clinical office experience, and a caring, empathetic, attentive approach that aligns with AWA's focus on youth wellness. Kind regards,

Jessica DiBiasio

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Adolescent Mental Health Program Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a senior nursing student at Binghamton University with experience in mental health advocacy, adolescent support, education, and healthcare settings, I am especially interested in the opportunity to support teens and families as they begin and navigate mental health care. I am also fluent in Spanish and English and have experience providing Korean–Spanish–English translation in healthcare and community settings.

My experience with adolescent mental health began through Medi-You, a virtual mental health initiative I founded. My nursing education has further developed my ability to communicate professionally, document accurately, work as part of a healthcare team, and recognize when concerns need to be escalated. During my clinical rotations, I have worked with pediatric, obstetric, medical-surgical, and geriatric patients and have practiced communicating with patients and families while providing safe, patient-centered care. I understand that this position is non-clinical and would maintain appropriate boundaries by bringing safety concerns, disclosures, or significant changes in behavior to the appropriate clinical team rather than attempting to address them outside my role.

I would also bring strong organizational and communication skills to the position. As a Binghamton University Student Ambassador, I communicate information to diverse audiences, guide families through important decisions, and collaborate with university staff to ensure smooth operations. My previous project and event coordination experience has also strengthened my ability to manage schedules, attendance, communication, and multiple responsibilities at once.

I would be excited to bring my background in nursing, adolescent mental health advocacy, education, and bilingual communication to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am organized, compassionate, dependable, and comfortable working with young people and families in situations that require patience, professionalism, and sound judgment. Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how I could contribute to your team.

Kind regards,
Yeon Ju Kim
